Lessons.Title: Which One Doesn’t Belong?
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will analyze numbers, expressions, geometric figures, and computations, identify your shared features and unique features, and use your analyses to complete or create Which One Doesn’t Belong sets.
This lesson allows you to apply your knowledge of various mathematical ideas from this course in generative ways. You examine sets of numbers, expressions, figures, or calculations, identify both shared and unique features, and create new items to complete Which One Doesn’t Belong sets. In the warm-up, you are given a full set of items.

2021 source activity sequence: Warm-up: Which One Doesn’t Belong: Strings of Numbers (10 minutes); Activity 1: Add One That Doesn’t Belong (20 minutes); Activity 2: Add Two That Don’t Belong (15 minutes); Activity 3: Add Three That Don’t Belong [OPTIONAL] (30 minutes); Cool-down: Reflection (5 minutes)
Math focus: A Which One Doesn't Belong? choice needs an explicit mathematical distinguishing feature; more than one defensible answer may exist.

Worked Edulytics example: Inspect all original numbers, expressions and figures before selecting an item. Name a feature shared by several entries and a feature excluding the chosen one. Explain the chosen answer with precise numerical, structural or geometric evidence. For 4, 6, 8, 9, only 9 is odd; different sets may have multiple valid reasons.
First-party Edulytics Cool-down (publisher's original not inspected): In 4, 6, 8 and 9, identify one item that differs and justify.
Original models, source figures, student-authored problems and teacher-scored explanations require separate academic review.
